action: Do not use nondihydropyridine calcium channel blockers in HFrEF
action_detail: Nondihydropyridine calcium channel blockers (diltiazem and verapamil) are myocardial depressants and are not recommended in HFrEF. Diltiazem was associated with higher risk of recurrent HF post-MI; verapamil had no survival benefit. Class III (Harm), LOE A.
source_text: In patients with HFrEF, nondihydropyridine calcium channel-blocking drugs are not recommended. (Class III: Harm, LOE A). Diltiazem and verapamil are myocardial depressants and generally not well tolerated in HF.

action: Do not use class IC antiarrhythmics or dronedarone in HFrEF
action_detail: Class IC antiarrhythmic medications (encainide, flecainide) and dronedarone may increase the risk of mortality in patients with HFrEF. CAST trial showed increased mortality with encainide/flecainide post-MI. ANDROMEDA trial showed increased mortality with dronedarone in hospitalized HFrEF. Class III (Harm), LOE A.
source_text: In patients with HFrEF, class IC antiarrhythmic medications and dronedarone may increase the risk of mortality. (Class III: Harm, LOE A)

action: Do not use thiazolidinediones in HFrEF
action_detail: Thiazolidinediones (rosiglitazone, pioglitazone) increase the risk of worsening HF symptoms and hospitalizations in patients with HFrEF. They activate PPARgamma which regulates sodium reabsorption causing fluid retention. Associated with increased HF events in patients with or without prior HF history. Class III (Harm), LOE A.
source_text: In patients with HFrEF, thiazolidinediones increase the risk of worsening HF symptoms and hospitalizations. (Class III: Harm, LOE A)

action: Avoid saxagliptin and alogliptin in patients with HF
action_detail: The DPP-4 inhibitors saxagliptin and alogliptin increase the risk of HF hospitalization in patients with type 2 diabetes and high cardiovascular risk. FDA recommends discontinuation in patients who develop HF. Whether risk is a class effect of all DPP-4 inhibitors is unclear; sitagliptin and linagliptin did not show increased risk. Class III (Harm), LOE B-R.
source_text: In patients with type 2 diabetes and high cardiovascular risk, the DPP-4 inhibitors saxagliptin and alogliptin increase the risk of HF hospitalization and should be avoided in patients with HF. (Class III: Harm, LOE B-R)

action: Avoid NSAIDs in patients with HFrEF
action_detail: NSAIDs (both nonselective and COX-2 selective) worsen HF symptoms through prostaglandin inhibition leading to sodium and water retention, increased systemic vascular resistance, and blunted response to diuretics. Several observational cohort studies revealed increased morbidity and mortality in HF patients using either nonselective or selective NSAIDs. Should be avoided or withdrawn whenever possible. Class III (Harm), LOE B-NR.

properties.mechanism: prostaglandin inhibition causing sodium/water retention, increased SVR, blunted diuretic response

source_text: In patients with HFrEF, NSAIDs worsen HF symptoms and should be avoided or withdrawn whenever possible. (Class III: Harm, LOE B-NR)

action: Dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers provide no benefit for HFrEF treatment
action_detail: Dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers (amlodipine, felodipine) are not recommended as treatment for HFrEF. PRAISE-1 showed potential benefit in nonischemic cardiomyopathy subgroup but PRAISE-2 found no survival benefit. However, they may be used for hypertension management if blood pressure remains elevated despite GDMT optimization. Class III (No Benefit), LOE A.
source_text: In patients with HFrEF, dihydropyridine calcium channel-blocking drugs are not recommended treatment for HF. (Class III: No Benefit, LOE A). PRAISE-2 showed no survival benefit in nonischemic cardiomyopathy.

action: Vitamins, nutritional supplements, and hormonal therapy are not recommended for HFrEF
action_detail: In patients with HFrEF, vitamins (D, E), nutritional supplements (coenzyme Q10, thiamine, carnitine, taurine), and hormonal therapies (testosterone, growth hormone, thyroid hormone) are not recommended except to correct specific deficiencies. Vitamin E may cause potential harm. Most studies limited by small sample sizes, surrogate endpoints, or nonrandomized design. Class III (No Benefit), LOE B-R.
